items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was now a papa because Joan was with Beezie and I. ... When Joan saw me giving up everything that I had downed earlier in the afternoon, she asked me in a very pitiful but cute voice, 'Are you sick also Daddy?'

ctx.x: One day I was out riding the bicycle with some of the gang and I was going along a very speedy pace. There are special sidewalks along many of the roads in Belgium and Holland for bicycles but in some places these special roads for bicycles come to an end and you are riding on regular road again. That was the case that day but after a little while I saw that the bicycle road started again. I was going so fast that I missed the entrance and when I realised that I was going to fall, the first thing I thought about…

After six weeks in Knocke we went to the Ostende Casino for two weeks. Beezie's daughter Joan who was 4 years old was living with her father in New York and Beezie received a letter saying that someone in Joan's father's family had some incurable illness and they were going to send Joan to us. Joan was due to arrive a week before we finished at Ostende, so Beezie came back to Paris a week before me.
We went into Florence for a short stay because Willie was engaged to play at a pavillion for the great Paris fair of 1937.
